newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close lower in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close lower in thin volume.

text.p: Malaysian shares remained weak until the close on continued lack of buying coupled with some selling by foreign funds, analysts and dealers said.
The benchmark Composite Index closed 7.08 points lower at 1,089.45. For the week, it was down 15.13 points.
Market volume stood at 236 million shares.

"The thin volume shows there's not much interest by institutional investors, both foreign and local," said Seow Choong Liang, managing director of Kleinwort Benson Research (Malaysia). "It will take a while for the market to recover. There's not enough positive momentum at the moment."
At best, the Composite Index will trade between 1,100 and 1,120, Seow said.
Phua Lee Kerk, head of research at Jupiter Securities, said that though he believed the worst was over, there was no sign of buyers returning to the market.
"Nobody is willing to make the first move," he said.
Analysts said investors were still digesting the impact of the recent move by Malaysia's central bank to curb financing to the property sector and for share purchases.
Phua expects the benchmark index to be supported at 1,070-1,080.
